events.title: Sundar Pichai named Google CEO
events.summary: Google appointed Sundar Pichai CEO on August 10, 2015 as Alphabet reorganized — putting him in charge of search, [Chrome], and [Android].
events.about: Pichai steered Google through the mobile-to-AI transition — scaling [Android], [Chrome], and later [Gemini]. He represents the product-engineer path to leading the world's largest internet software stack.

narrative.whyChosen: Pichai leads the company whose platforms most developers build on or compete with.
narrative.whyImportant: His tenure spans mobile dominance and the [generative AI] race.
narrative.problemSolved: Google needed focused product leadership after the Alphabet split from experimental bets.

events.title: Samsung Galaxy Note 5 released
events.summary: Samsung released the Samsung Galaxy Note 5 — glass unibody design — dropped microSD in favor of premium build.
events.about: The Galaxy Note targeted stylus power users on [Android]. Glass unibody design — dropped microsd in favor of premium build. Note apps and split-screen [Android] development often targeted this hardware class.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy Note 5 advanced Samsung's stylus phablet line.
narrative.whyImportant: Galaxy Note hardware defined large-screen [Android] productivity for years.
narrative.problemSolved: [Android] lacked a premium large-screen stylus flagship for note-taking workflows.

events.title: Phoenix 1.0 released
events.summary: Chris McCord released Phoenix 1.0 on August 28, 2015 — a productive [Elixir] web framework with channels for real-time WebSocket apps.
events.about: Phoenix brought Rails-like productivity to [Elixir]: generators, Ecto for databases, and channels for live updates. It powered Discord-scale chat, dashboards, and APIs where [BEAM] fault tolerance mattered — proving [Elixir] was more than a syntax experiment.

narrative.whyChosen: Phoenix 1.0 was the web framework that made [Elixir] production-credible.
narrative.whyImportant: Channels and [OTP] supervision brought real-time features without fragile [Node] clusters.
narrative.problemSolved: [Elixir] needed a batteries-included web stack to compete with Rails and Django.

events.title: Ashley Madison user data leaked
events.summary: The Impact Team published a 9.7 GB dump of Ashley Madison customer data on August 18, 2015 — exposing millions of accounts from the extramarital dating site.
events.about: The Impact Team breach dumped emails, credit cards, and internal source code — demonstrating that even adult sites storing secrets face extortion and reputational ruin. It accelerated debates over data retention, [bcrypt] versus weak hashing, and whether security teams owe duty of care to users engaging in sensitive behavior.

narrative.whyChosen: Ashley Madison was the hack that proved no niche site was too embarrassing to target.
narrative.whyImportant: It highlighted weak password storage and destructive hacktivist motives.
narrative.problemSolved: Nothing for users — it exposed that 'discreet' marketing did not mean secure engineering.
